questions.prompt: An inconsistent linear system has:
explanations: A system with exactly one solution is consistent and independent.
A system with infinitely many solutions is consistent and dependent.
Free variables mean infinitely many solutions — the system is still consistent.

questions.prompt: A homogeneous linear system $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$ is always:
explanations: Homogeneous systems always have at least the trivial solution $\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$, so they can never be inconsistent.
It may be independent (unique solution) or dependent (infinitely many) — but consistent either way.
Being homogeneous says nothing about the form of the matrix.

questions.prompt: The augmented matrix of a system with $n$ variables has how many columns?
choices: Depends on the number of equations
explanations: The coefficient matrix has $n$ columns, but the augmented matrix adds one more for the right-hand side.
That would be fewer columns than variables — not correct.
The number of columns in an augmented matrix is always $n+1$, regardless of the number of equations.

questions.prompt: The number of variables in a linear system corresponds to the number of _____ in the coefficient matrix.
explanations: Rows correspond to equations, not variables.
The number of pivots tells you the rank, not directly the number of variables.
Equations correspond to rows, not variables.

questions.prompt: How many solutions can a consistent linear system have?
choices: Either exactly one or infinitely many
explanations: A consistent system can also have infinitely many solutions.
Linear systems can never have exactly two solutions.
Linear systems obey the 0-1-infinity rule — never a finite number other than 0 or 1.

questions.prompt: A linear system where the solution contains free variables is called:
explanations: Inconsistent means no solution at all — free variables indicate a solution exists.
Independent means exactly one solution — no free variables.
Homogeneous means all constants are zero — unrelated to having free variables.

questions.prompt: In a system of 2 equations in 2 unknowns, each equation geometrically represents a:
explanations: A point is a solution, not an equation.
Planes arise in 3-variable systems.
Hyperplanes arise in 4+ variable systems.

questions.prompt: Each equation in a system of 3 equations in 3 unknowns geometrically represents a:
explanations: Lines in $\mathbb{R}^3$ require two equations to pin down, not one.
A point is a solution, not a single equation.
Spheres are not linear — they involve squared terms.

questions.prompt: A system with 5 equations and 3 unknowns:
choices: Must be inconsistent because there are more equations than unknowns
Must be consistent because there are enough equations
explanations: Having more equations than unknowns does not guarantee inconsistency — some equations may be redundant.
More equations can actually make it harder to be consistent, not easier.
With more equations than unknowns it is unlikely (but not impossible) to have infinitely many solutions.

questions.prompt: Which augmented matrix represents an inconsistent system?
explanations: This is consistent — back substitution gives a unique solution.
This is consistent with a free variable — infinitely many solutions.
This is consistent — a unique solution exists.

questions.prompt: Consider the augmented matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1&4\\0&1&3&2\\0&0&0&0\end{bmatrix}$. How many free variables are there?
explanations: There is at least one non-pivot column among the variable columns.
There are 3 variable columns and 2 pivots, giving only 1 free variable.
Three free variables would mean no pivots at all.

questions.prompt: The trivial solution to a homogeneous system $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ is:
choices: Any vector in the null space
explanations: Plugging in all ones does not generally satisfy a homogeneous system.
The null space contains all solutions including non-trivial ones — the trivial solution is specifically $\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$.
Every homogeneous system has the trivial solution.

questions.prompt: A system has the augmented matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&0&3\\0&1&-2\end{bmatrix}$. What is the solution?
explanations: The last column of the augmented matrix is the right-hand side — sign error here.
The zero vector is not the solution unless the system is homogeneous and trivial.
With two pivots for two variables there are no free variables, so the solution is unique.

questions.prompt: Which of these systems is homogeneous?
explanations: The right-hand side is 3, not 0.
The first equation has right-hand side 1, not 0.
This is a contradiction — inconsistent, not homogeneous.

questions.prompt: If a linear system has a unique solution, it is:
explanations: Inconsistent means no solution — contradicts having a unique solution.
Dependent means infinitely many solutions — contradicts unique.
Homogeneous is a separate property about the right-hand side, not about uniqueness.

questions.prompt: Row operations on an augmented matrix:
choices: Must be done in a specific fixed order
explanations: Row operations are chosen precisely because they do NOT change the solution set.
Row reduction works on any matrix regardless of shape.
The order of row operations can vary — many valid sequences lead to RREF.

questions.prompt: A system of 2 equations in 3 unknowns can have:
choices: No solution or infinitely many solutions
explanations: With more unknowns than equations (and no contradiction), there will always be free variables.
Linear systems never have exactly two solutions.
The trivial solution only applies to homogeneous systems.

questions.prompt: The row $\begin{bmatrix}0&0&0&5\end{bmatrix}$ in an augmented matrix means the system is:
explanations: This row says $0 = 5$, which is a contradiction — no free variable can fix this.
Homogeneous systems have all zeros on the right — this has a 5.
Independent means a unique solution — impossible with a contradiction present.

questions.prompt: Three planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ have infinitely many intersection points. Which configuration is NOT possible?
choices: The planes intersect along a common line
The planes intersect at exactly 2 points
The planes form a consistent dependent system
explanations: Three identical planes give a consistent dependent system with infinitely many solutions.
Intersecting along a line gives infinitely many solutions — this is possible.
Consistent dependent systems are exactly the case of infinitely many solutions.

questions.prompt: An $m \times n$ augmented matrix represents a system with:
explanations: Rows correspond to equations, columns to variables — these are swapped.
Close, but the augmented matrix has one extra column for the right-hand side.
The extra column is in the column direction, not the row direction.

questions.prompt: The system $\begin{cases}x_1 + x_2 = 4 \\ 2x_1 + 2x_2 = 8\end{cases}$ has:
explanations: The second equation is just twice the first — it adds no new information, so solutions exist.
The second equation is redundant, leaving one free variable.
Linear systems never have exactly two solutions.

questions.prompt: What does it mean for $(x_1, x_2, x_3) = (1, 0, -2)$ to be a solution to a system?
choices: It satisfies at least one equation in the system
It satisfies all equations in the system simultaneously
explanations: A solution must satisfy ALL equations, not just one.
There may be other solutions — being a solution doesn't imply uniqueness.
The trivial solution has all zeros — $(1,0,-2)$ has nonzero entries.

questions.prompt: A homogeneous system with more unknowns than equations:
choices: Is always in row echelon form
explanations: Homogeneous systems are always consistent — they always have $\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$.
More unknowns than equations guarantees at least one free variable, so there are non-trivial solutions.
Row echelon form is a property of the matrix, not of the system type.

questions.prompt: The system represented by $\begin{bmatrix}1&-2&1&0\\0&1&-3&0\\0&0&0&0\end{bmatrix}$ is homogeneous and has:
explanations: There is a free variable ($x_3$), so non-trivial solutions exist.
Homogeneous systems always have at least the trivial solution.
Linear systems never have exactly two solutions.

questions.prompt: The coefficient matrix of the system $\begin{cases}2x_1 - x_2 + 3x_3 = 5 \\ x_1 + 4x_3 = -1\end{cases}$ is:
explanations: This is the augmented matrix — it includes the right-hand side constants.
This drops the $x_3$ column — missing coefficients.
This is just the right-hand side vector, not the coefficient matrix.

questions.prompt: Which matrix is the augmented matrix for $\begin{cases}3x_1 + x_2 = 7 \\ -x_1 + 2x_2 = 4\end{cases}$?
explanations: This is only the coefficient matrix — missing the right-hand side column.
The constants belong in the last column, and the rows correspond to equations.
The rows and columns are transposed — each row should represent one equation.

questions.prompt: A $4 \times 6$ augmented matrix represents a system with how many equations and how many unknowns?
explanations: Rows = equations is correct, but columns in an augmented matrix = unknowns + 1.
Rows are equations, not columns.
Both counts are wrong here.

questions.prompt: If a consistent system has no free variables, it has:
explanations: Consistent means at least one solution exists.
Infinitely many solutions require at least one free variable.
No free variables means the solution is fully determined — exactly one.

questions.prompt: A linear system where all right-hand sides equal zero is called _____.
questions.explanation: Homogeneous means $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ — every equation in the system equals zero on the right-hand side.

questions.prompt: A system with no solution is called _____.
questions.explanation: Inconsistent means the system has no solution — the equations contradict each other.

questions.prompt: A system with infinitely many solutions is called consistent and _____.
questions.explanation: When a consistent system has free variables it has infinitely many solutions and is called dependent.

questions.prompt: The solution of ALL zeros to a homogeneous system is called the _____ solution.
questions.explanation: The trivial solution is $\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ — it always exists for homogeneous systems and requires no work to find.

questions.prompt: Variables that can take any value in the solution of a dependent system are called _____ variables.
questions.explanation: Free variables correspond to non-pivot columns — they are unconstrained and parameterize the infinite solution set.

questions.prompt: The matrix formed by the coefficients of the variables only (no right-hand side) is the _____ matrix.
questions.explanation: The coefficient matrix contains only the coefficients of the variables. Adding the right-hand side column produces the augmented matrix.

questions.prompt: Adding the right-hand-side constants as an extra column to the coefficient matrix gives the _____ matrix.
questions.explanation: The augmented matrix $[A \mid \mathbf{b}]$ appends the right-hand side vector to the coefficient matrix, encoding the full system.

questions.prompt: A system with exactly one solution is called consistent and _____.
questions.explanation: Independent means no free variables — the solution is uniquely determined.

questions.prompt: Given the augmented matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&0&-1&3\\0&1&2&-5\\0&0&1&4\end{bmatrix}$. How many unknowns does this system have?
questions.explanation: The augmented matrix has 4 columns. The last column is the right-hand side, so the number of unknowns = 4 - 1 = 3.

questions.prompt: How many equations does the system represented by $\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3&0\\0&4&-1&2\\0&0&5&-3\end{bmatrix}$ have?
questions.explanation: The number of equations equals the number of rows — this matrix has 3 rows, so 3 equations.

questions.prompt: Given the augmented matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&3&-2&5\\0&0&1&3\end{bmatrix}$. How many free variables are there?
questions.explanation: There are 3 variable columns and 2 pivot columns ($x_1$ and $x_3$). That leaves $3 - 2 = 1$ free variable ($x_2$).

questions.prompt: From the augmented matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0&7\\0&1&0&-3\\0&0&1&2\end{bmatrix}$, what is the value of $x_2$?
questions.explanation: In RREF the solution can be read directly: $x_1=7$, $x_2=-3$, $x_3=2$.

questions.prompt: From the system $\begin{cases}x_1 = 5 \\ x_2 = -2 \\ x_3 = 0\end{cases}$, what is $x_3$?
questions.explanation: The system is already solved: $x_3 = 0$.

questions.prompt: A coefficient matrix has 4 columns. How many variables does the system have?
questions.explanation: Each column of the coefficient matrix corresponds to one variable.

questions.prompt: An augmented matrix has 5 columns. How many unknowns does the system have?
questions.explanation: The augmented matrix has one extra column for the right-hand side, so unknowns = columns - 1 = 4.

questions.prompt: How many solutions does an inconsistent system have?
questions.explanation: Inconsistent means no solution — the equations are contradictory.

questions.prompt: A $3 \times 5$ coefficient matrix represents a system with how many variables?
questions.explanation: Columns of the coefficient matrix = number of variables = 5.

questions.prompt: A $3 \times 5$ coefficient matrix represents a system with how many equations?
questions.explanation: Rows of any matrix = number of equations = 3.

questions.prompt: Solve for $x_1$: the system has augmented matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&4\\0&1&3\end{bmatrix}$ in REF. Using back-substitution with $x_2 = 3$: what is $x_1$?
questions.explanation: From row 1: $x_1 + 2(3) = 4 \Rightarrow x_1 + 6 = 4 \Rightarrow x_1 = -2$.

questions.prompt: True or False: Every homogeneous system is consistent.
explanations: Homogeneous systems always have $\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ as a solution, so they are always consistent.

questions.prompt: True or False: The number of columns of the augmented matrix equals the number of variables.
explanations: The augmented matrix has one extra column for the right-hand side constants.

questions.prompt: True or False: The number of rows of the coefficient matrix equals the number of variables.
explanations: Rows correspond to equations, not variables. Columns correspond to variables.

questions.prompt: True or False: A solution to a system must satisfy all equations in the system simultaneously.
explanations: Satisfying only some equations is not sufficient — all equations must be satisfied.

questions.prompt: True or False: A linear system can have exactly 2 solutions.
explanations: Linear systems obey the 0-1-infinity rule: no solution, exactly one, or infinitely many. Never exactly 2.

questions.prompt: True or False: A system of 2 equations in 4 variables can have no solution.
explanations: Even with fewer equations than unknowns, the equations could still contradict each other.

questions.prompt: True or False: If a 3×3 system is consistent, the three planes must intersect at exactly one point.
explanations: They could also intersect along a line (infinitely many solutions) or even all coincide.

questions.prompt: True or False: Each equation in a 3-variable system represents a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
explanations: A single linear equation in 3 variables $ax_1+bx_2+cx_3=d$ defines a plane, not a line.

questions.prompt: True or False: If a system has more equations than unknowns, it must be inconsistent.
explanations: Extra equations can be redundant — for example, $x=1$ and $2x=2$ is consistent with two equations and one unknown.

questions.prompt: True or False: A system with infinitely many solutions has at least one free variable.
explanations: Free variables are exactly what allow infinitely many solutions — each one adds a dimension of freedom.

questions.prompt: True or False: A system with a free variable must be homogeneous.
explanations: Non-homogeneous systems can also have free variables and infinitely many solutions.

questions.prompt: True or False: A homogeneous system with more unknowns than equations always has infinitely many solutions.
explanations: More unknowns than equations guarantees at least one free variable, meaning non-trivial solutions always exist.

questions.prompt: True or False: The row $[0\ 0\ 0\ |\ 3]$ in an augmented matrix means the system is inconsistent.
explanations: This row represents $0x_1 + 0x_2 + 0x_3 = 3$, i.e., $0 = 3$ — a contradiction, so the system is inconsistent.

questions.prompt: True or False: Elementary row operations can change whether a system is consistent or inconsistent.
explanations: Elementary row operations preserve the solution set exactly — they never change consistency.

questions.prompt: True or False: The coefficient matrix and augmented matrix always have the same number of rows.
explanations: Both matrices have one row per equation — the augmented matrix just has one extra column, not row.

questions.prompt: True or False: A consistent system with 4 unknowns and 2 pivot columns has 2 free variables.
explanations: Free variables = unknowns − pivot columns = 4 − 2 = 2.

questions.prompt: True or False: The system $\begin{cases}x_1 + x_2 = 3 \\ 2x_1 + 2x_2 = 7\end{cases}$ is consistent.
explanations: Multiply the first equation by 2: $2x_1 + 2x_2 = 6 \neq 7$ — contradiction. The system is inconsistent.

questions.prompt: Consider the system $\begin{cases}x_1 - 2x_2 + x_3 = 0 \\ 2x_1 + x_2 - x_3 = 0\end{cases}$. True or False: This is a homogeneous system.
explanations: Both equations equal 0 on the right-hand side — that is exactly the definition of homogeneous.

questions.prompt: True or False: In a system with 3 equations and 3 unknowns, if the determinant of the coefficient matrix is nonzero, the system has a unique solution.
explanations: Nonzero determinant means the matrix is invertible, guaranteeing a unique solution for any right-hand side.

questions.prompt: The system $\begin{cases}x_1 + 2x_2 = 5 \\ 3x_1 + 6x_2 = 15\end{cases}$ has what kind of solution set?
explanations: The second equation is just 3 times the first — they are not contradictory.
The second equation gives no new information, leaving one free variable.
Linear systems can never have exactly 3 solutions.

questions.prompt: If a $5 \times 3$ coefficient matrix (5 equations, 3 unknowns) has rank 3 after row reduction, the system:
choices: Has a unique solution if consistent
explanations: Rank 3 = 3 pivot columns = no free variables. If consistent, the solution is unique.
Rank 3 with 3 unknowns means no free variables. Whether it's consistent depends on the augmented matrix.
Free variables = unknowns − rank = 3 − 3 = 0.

questions.prompt: A system has augmented matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&2&3\\0&0&0&0\\0&0&0&0\end{bmatrix}$. It has:
explanations: There is no contradiction row — the system is consistent.
There are 2 non-pivot columns among the 3 variable columns — 2 free variables.
Linear systems never have exactly 2 solutions.

questions.prompt: The system $\begin{cases}x_1 - x_2 = 4 \\ -2x_1 + 2x_2 = -8\end{cases}$: after row reducing, what does the second row become?
explanations: The second equation is exactly $-2$ times the first — adding twice row 1 to row 2 gives all zeros.
That's the second row before row reduction.
Sign error — the correct operation gives a zero row, not a pivot on $x_2$.

questions.prompt: A student says: 'This system has 3 equations and 4 unknowns, so it must have infinitely many solutions.' Is this correct?
choices: Yes — fewer equations than unknowns always means infinitely many solutions
No — the system could also be inconsistent
Yes — as long as the system is homogeneous
No — it could also have a unique solution
explanations: If the system is inconsistent, there are no solutions at all — the student is forgetting this case.
Even homogeneous systems with more unknowns have infinitely many solutions — but the student's claim includes non-homogeneous systems that could be inconsistent.
With more unknowns than equations, a unique solution is impossible (at least one free variable would remain).

questions.prompt: Which statement about a $3 \times 3$ homogeneous system is always true?
choices: It has only the trivial solution
It has at least one solution
It is in row echelon form
explanations: It could have only the trivial solution if the coefficient matrix is invertible.
It could also have infinitely many solutions if the matrix is singular.
Row echelon form is a property of the matrix representation, not of the system type.

questions.prompt: A system is called _____ if it has at least one solution.
questions.explanation: Consistent simply means the system has at least one solution — it could be one solution or infinitely many.

questions.prompt: In a linear system, each equation corresponds to one _____ of the coefficient matrix.
questions.explanation: Each equation in a linear system becomes one row when we write it as a matrix. Columns correspond to variables.

questions.prompt: A system $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ where $\mathbf{b} \neq \mathbf{0}$ is called _____.
questions.explanation: When the right-hand side is not the zero vector, the system is non-homogeneous (also called inhomogeneous).

questions.prompt: The set of all solutions to a linear system is called the _____ set.
questions.explanation: The solution set contains every ordered tuple that satisfies all equations in the system simultaneously.

questions.prompt: A system has 2 equations and 2 unknowns. Geometrically each equation is a line. If the lines are parallel and distinct, how many solutions does the system have?
questions.explanation: Parallel distinct lines never intersect — so there is no point satisfying both equations, meaning no solution.

questions.prompt: Two lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$ that are identical (the same line) represent a system with _____ solutions.
questions.explanation: Identical lines share every point — so every point on the line satisfies both equations, giving infinitely many solutions.

questions.prompt: For $(x_1, x_2) = (3, -1)$ to be a solution to a system, it must satisfy _____ equations in the system.
questions.explanation: A solution must satisfy every equation simultaneously — satisfying only some is not enough.

questions.prompt: A system has 3 unknowns and its augmented matrix has 4 columns. How many columns does its coefficient matrix have?
questions.explanation: The augmented matrix adds one column (for the right-hand side) to the coefficient matrix. So coefficient matrix columns = 4 - 1 = 3.

questions.prompt: Two lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$ intersect at exactly one point. The corresponding system is:
explanations: Inconsistent means no intersection — but these lines do intersect.
Dependent means infinitely many solutions — one intersection point means exactly one solution.
Homogeneous refers to the right-hand side being zero — unrelated to how many intersections exist.

questions.prompt: Three planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that all pass through the origin:
choices: Must intersect only at the origin
explanations: Planes through the origin always share at least the origin — so the system is consistent.
They could also share an entire line or plane through the origin.
They could intersect along a whole line or plane, giving infinitely many solutions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the solution set of a dependent system?
choices: A line, plane, or higher-dimensional set
explanations: The empty set describes an inconsistent system.
A single point means exactly one solution — that's an independent system.
Linear systems can never have exactly two solutions.

questions.prompt: A system of equations where every equation has the form $a_1x_1 + a_2x_2 + \cdots + a_nx_n = 0$ is:
explanations: Homogeneous systems always have the trivial solution — they are never inconsistent.
Independent refers to having a unique solution — a separate property.
All equations are linear — they have the form of a linear combination equal to zero.

questions.prompt: If $(2, -1, 3)$ is a solution to a system, then substituting $x_1=2$, $x_2=-1$, $x_3=3$:
choices: Satisfies all equations in the system
Only works if the system is homogeneous
explanations: A solution must satisfy ALL equations, not just some.
A solution satisfies every equation, not just one.
A solution is defined for any system — homogeneous or not.

questions.prompt: True or False: A non-homogeneous system can never have the zero vector as a solution.
explanations: A non-homogeneous system $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ with $\mathbf{b}\neq\mathbf{0}$ gives $A\mathbf{0}=\mathbf{0}\neq\mathbf{b}$, so $\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ is never a solution.

questions.prompt: True or False: Two different linear systems can have exactly the same solution set.
explanations: Systems that are multiples of each other, or that differ by row operations, can have identical solution sets.

questions.prompt: True or False: A system with fewer equations than unknowns can have a unique solution.
explanations: With fewer equations than unknowns there will always be at least one free variable, making a unique solution impossible.

questions.prompt: True or False: The trivial solution always satisfies a homogeneous system.
explanations: $A\mathbf{0} = \mathbf{0}$ is always true — the trivial solution satisfies every homogeneous system.

questions.prompt: True or False: A $2 \times 4$ coefficient matrix (2 equations, 4 unknowns) can represent a consistent system.
explanations: The system is consistent as long as the equations don't contradict each other — the size alone doesn't force inconsistency.

questions.prompt: The system $\begin{cases}x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = 0 \\ 2x_1 - x_2 + x_3 = 0 \\ -x_1 + 3x_2 - x_3 = 0\end{cases}$ is homogeneous. What can we say immediately?
choices: It has at least one solution: $x_1=x_2=x_3=0$
explanations: Homogeneous systems always have at least the trivial solution.
We know the trivial solution exists, but without more work we can't rule out other solutions.
It may or may not have non-trivial solutions — that requires further analysis.

questions.prompt: A system has augmented matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1&5\\0&0&3&6\\0&0&0&0\end{bmatrix}$. What is the value of $x_3$?
explanations: 6 is the right-hand side, not the solution — divide: $3x_3=6$ so $x_3=2$.
3 is the coefficient of $x_3$, not the value.
The zero row gives no information about $x_3$ — use the second row.
